title: Copyrighting under his own name and Shields's collaboration
summary: He explains he put tunes under his own name because bandmates took royalties, and discusses Shields as collaborator.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you why I did that. The reason I did that, because I had so many numbers on my name. And I had to share with the guys in the band. You understand what I mean? I tried to look out for myself. Up to this time, these fellas rode my back. They composed not only with Shields, who collaborated on some of the numbers. Rager's name is on some of them. But he did nothing but just hold the chords down on the piano, which I gave him to play. Shields collaborated. And on the numbers that Shields collaborated, he's got his name on there. Now, I'm trying to break away from this and get money for myself. I'd seen the handwriting on the wall that some of the fellas wouldn't work. All they were doing was taking the royalties, getting the royalties, contributing nothing to their music. How would you feel? Then I started putting out popular numbers, Summer, Rainy Night. Their name was not on that either. Ramblin' Blues, their name was not on that. Just Shields I, and I had my names on that.
But Shields was a real collaborator. Yes.

Shields collaborated from the beginning. Not from the beginning. I had four tunes out before Shields ever collaborated. But his name was on the Ostrich Walk. But I had them numbers before I left New Orleans. I brought them there. Now, these guys say they played these numbers. Possibly they did. How many bands did I play with? I jumped off this breakdown here. You questioned me. That's how I got to know how to form melodies against a chord construction. And from that on, I was on my own. Now, where was the back on the other side? We were talking about the collaboration of Shields.

But that begins in New York. He collaborated on jazz band Ball. On the fidgety feet. And I think, yeah, because the client at Marmalade was one of my numbers. And he collaborated on that. Just he and Regis' name on that. See, because every one of the names on it, the guys were getting jealous. They think that my name shouldn't, their name shouldn't be on that. So I put one of their names on it. And you're bringing me into a place a little ahead of time. But I just want to go on to it now. So, Liverstable Blues. The Ostrich Walks, which was then in New Orleans. I call that Taddy Eagles and that's down. One was named Hunyadi.
